key_insight: MM-CondChain is a programmatically verified benchmark that evaluates MLLMs on deeply chained, visually grounded conditional reasoning with branching and early termination — exposing failures that shallow or independent-constraint benchmarks miss.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks do not test long chains of visual conditions, branching logic, and early termination as found in real visual workflows (e.g., GUI navigation), so models appear capable on simple tasks but fail on true compositional control flow.
method: Construct a benchmark (MM-CondChain) of visually grounded workflows that require verifying multistep compositional conditions, branching decisions, and possible early exits.
Implement a programmatic verifier that checks each step's visual condition against ground-truth observations to ensure precise correctness (not just final-action similarity).
Provide an evaluation protocol that measures performance by composition depth, branching complexity, and correct termination handling to reveal nuanced failure modes.
impact: Provides practitioners a targeted way to diagnose and improve MLLMs for real-world visual control tasks (e.g., GUI automation, assistive agents) and to measure robustness and safety when decisions depend on chained visual conditions.
visual_elements: Flowchart showing a conditional chain with branches and early termination (example: permission dialog -> color check -> click/stop).
Example GUI snapshots annotated with the visual conditions to be verified at each step.
Bar/line chart comparing model performance by composition depth and branching complexity.
Diagram of the programmatic verification pipeline (input image + model action -> verifier -> pass/fail).
paper_title: MM-CondChain: A Programmatically Verified Benchmark for Visually Grounded Deep Compositional Reasoning
paper_authors: Haozhan Shen, Shilin Yan, Hongwei Xue, Shuaiqi Lu, Xiaojun Tang
